newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ministry lifts restrictions on Daiwa Bank.
newsitem.headline: Japan ministry lifts restrictions on Daiwa Bank.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry said Monday it had lifted restrictions it imposed on Daiwa Bank Ltd last year after the bank revealed huge losses from unauthorised trades at its New York branch.

Daiwa Bank -- one of Japan's top commercial banks -- pleaded guilty in February 1996 to charges of hiding a $1.1 billion loss from the trades and agreed to pay $340 million in fines, the biggest criminal fine ever levied against a financial firm in the United States.
The debacle rocked confidence in Japanese banks and tarnished the Finance Ministry's reputation when it became known that it was informed of the loss before U.S. authorities were notified.
In November 1995, U.S. regulatory authorities ordered Daiwa to close its operations in the United States and instigated the lawsuits, which resulted in Daiwa's guilty plea and fine.
The Finance Ministry then issued orders to Daiwa including instructions to streamline its overseas operations, establish sound management practices and suspend the setting up of overseas branches.

A Finance Ministry official said Monday that all the orders to Daiwa had been lifted, including a one-year restriction on its overseas foreign exchange business that expired automatically at the end of October.

After the lifting of other orders on Monday, Daiwa can open overseas branches, buy stocks of companies affilated with Japanese firms and make new overseas trust contracts as a trustee. The move followed a recent inspection of the bank by the ministry, another official said.
Daiwa said Friday that it posted a parent net profit of 11.99 billion yen ($107 million) in the six months to Sept. 30, up from 7.33 billion yen ($65.4 million) for the same period last year.
